tokyo_asakusa_monja_okonomiyak.price_note: Prices approximate — may change, and these are TAX-EXCLUSIVE: the list carries 「※表示価格は税抜きです」, so add 10% at the till. Item list is the shop's 公式 Tabelog registration, 更新日 2024/11/06 — over a year old, so treat the figures as indicative. The English street A-board photographed 2025/10 (¥4,000 for 2 drinks + 2 dishes) is current. The shop's own domain asakusa-ponchan.com no longer serves a site (HTTP 404). Tabelog's own おすすめ panel disagrees with its item list on two dishes — 明太子スペシャルもんじゃ appears at both ¥1,550 and ¥1,000, and 基本のお好み焼き at both ¥750 and ¥550; the section-list figure is used below.

items.en: Basic monja — cabbage, spring onion, dried squid, tempura crumbs, fried pork fat and dried shrimp, cooked by you on the griddle
items.section: もんじゃ＆お好み焼き Monja & okonomiyaki
items.note: Monjayaki is a loose 小麦粉 (wheat flour) batter thinned with dashi or Worcestershire-style sauce, and the listed base already includes 揚げ玉 (wheat tempura crumbs) and 油かす (fried pork fat). Wheat and pork; there is no version of this dish that is safe for either diet.

items.ja: 基本のお好み焼き 玉子入り
items.en: Basic okonomiyaki with egg — cabbage, spring onion, dried squid, tempura crumbs, pork fat, pickled ginger

items.note: Wheat-flour batter, egg, 揚げ玉 (wheat) and 油かす (pork). Okonomiyaki sauce is a Worcestershire-type sauce and okonomiyaki mayonnaise is egg. Tabelog's おすすめ panel prices this at ¥750; the section list says ¥550.

Wheat batter with seafood and meat.

items.en: Yakisoba — fried wheat noodles, toppings available

Salt instead of sauce, but the noodles are still wheat.
Listed on the shop's English street board (Yaki-Udon, 'Fride Udon') but not in the Tabelog price list, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed. Udon is wheat.
もろみ味噌 is a chunky fermented paste made from soybeans AND barley or wheat koji — a gluten grain by construction. Usually plant-only, but some versions add bonito.
Cucumber and umeboshi paste — plant-only in principle and no wheat ingredient, but commercial 梅肉 is often extended with bonito (かつお梅) or with mirin. Ask.
Kimchi in Japan almost always contains 魚醤 or salted shrimp/anchovy — not vegan. Gochujang, if present, is usually made with wheat flour, so gluten is a real question too.

Plain cut tomato — the only thing on this menu that is plant-only by construction. Gluten 'ask' rather than 'gf' because it is prepared in a kitchen whose entire output is wheat batter, and it is sometimes served with a mayonnaise or dressing on the side.

Liver, almost always simmered or dressed in a soy-and-mirin sauce.

items.en: Tekka-don — tuna sashimi over sushi rice
items.note: Raw tuna and rice only, so the bowl itself may be wheat-free — but it is served to be eaten with soy sauce and usually arrives with wasabi and a soy dressing. Ask for the fish plain and bring your own tamari.

items.en: Battera — Osaka-style pressed mackerel sushi, the shop's signature
items.note: The shop calls this its 名物. Battera is pressed cured mackerel over vinegared rice under a sheet of 白板昆布. The cure is salt + vinegar, so it can be wheat-free — but many shops add a little soy or mirin to the marinade and to the kombu sheet. Ask before eating; the shop publishes no allergen list.
Tuna, rice and nori are wheat-free in themselves, but the roll is served for dipping in wheat-brewed soy sauce.

items.ja: のり巻き(かんぴょう、梅じそ、かっぱ、たくわん、各種3本)
items.en: Nori rolls — kanpyo (gourd), ume-shiso, cucumber or takuwan pickle; 3 rolls of one kind
items.note: かっぱ (cucumber) and 梅じそ are plant-only fillings, but かんぴょう is simmered in soy sauce and sugar — wheat, and usually a bonito dashi. Takuwan is normally vegan but is often coloured/seasoned. Nothing here is safe for gluten; a cucumber roll eaten without soy sauce is the closest to vegan, so ask.
Raw fish with wasabi is naturally gluten-free; the risk is entirely the dipping soy sauce (wheat) and any shared board. Bring tamari and ask the counter to plate it without sauce.

items.en: Conger eel grilled plain ('white-grilled'), no glaze
items.note: 白焼き means grilled WITHOUT the soy-and-mirin ツメ glaze — the shop's own menu page contrasts it with 穴子のツメ. Salt-grilled eel can be wheat-free, but shirayaki is conventionally served with salt or wasabi-soy, and the same grill handles the glazed version. Confirm no tare touched it.
Boiled octopus, plain. Wheat risk is the soy dip only.
Kazunoko is desalted then steeped in a dashi-and-soy marinade (味付け数の子) in almost every sushi shop — soy is wheat and the dashi is bonito. Fish roe, so not vegan.

items.en: Squid tentacles, a small drinking snack

items.en: Soup bowl — freshwater clam miso soup

READ THE GLUTEN NOTE ON EVERY ITEM: the shop states in Japanese and English that its mochi contains wheat flour and is NOT gluten-free.

items.en: Mochi dusted with roasted soybean flour — the shop's number-one classic, 3 pieces
items.section: 定番もち Signature mochi (3 pieces)
items.note: CONTAINS WHEAT. The shop's own menu card footnote reads 「厳選した国産小麦をほんのわずかに使用しております。（特定原材料：小麦を含みます／グルテンフリーではございません）」 and the English page repeats it: 'we incorporate a small amount of premium Japanese wheat flour. (Contains: Wheat / Not Gluten-Free)'. Mochi is normally assumed safe — here it is not. Kinako and sugar are plant-only, so it is vegan but not coeliac-safe.
